studies.label: Map the failures
studies.title: First, understand where the system breaks.
studies.summary: A PRISMA-guided review of 61 studies organizes RAG failures into four groups: missing context, context noise, formatting errors, and hallucination despite retrieval. Pilot Arabic and Malay experiments help frame the next questions.

studies.label: Test the reward
studies.title: A stronger score is not always a better answer.
studies.summary: Five-seed experiments on Qwen3 and T5Gemma 2 isolate an NLI reward from fine-tuning and its surrounding machinery. After length matching, the reward provides no reliable additional benefit in the tested setting.

studies.label: What comes next
studies.title: Test mitigation under imperfect evidence.
studies.summary: The next study plans to compare length-controlled preference optimization and evidence-grounded training under distractors, missing evidence, and retrieval variation. Improved performance is a question to test, not an assumed result.
